newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt gets total NZ$108 mln for Works Corp.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt gets total NZ$108 mln for Works Corp.

text.p: The New Zealand government said on Tuesday it had sold state-owned engineering consultancy Works Corporation for a total of NZ$108 million.
The government said Works Consultancy was sold to Kinta Kellas, a member of Malaysia's Renong Group, for $45.8 million.
Works Civil Construction was sold to Downer and Company Ltd for NZ$44 million.
Kinta Kellas will also repay Consultancy's advances from Works in the order of $4.2 million and Downer will repay Civil's advances in the order of $14 million.

The value of Works shareholders' funds at June 30, 1996 was NZ$83 million, down from $98 million in the 1995 annual report, mainly as a result of a $15 million capital repayment during the financial year.
Downer is owned by Brierley Investments Ltd's 23 percent-owned associate Hong Kong-listed Paul Y-ITC.
State-Owned Enterprises Minister Philip Burdon called the sale price extremely good and confirmed the proceeds would be used to repay government debt.
"The real issue is the ability of the new owners to expand the businesses," he said. "They will globalise the business in a way we never could have done."

The New Zealand government's latest asset sale follows last week's announcement on the NZ$2 billion sale of Forestry Corporation to a consortium involving Fletcher Challenge Forest Division, Brierley and China's Citic.
